findings.text: crates/app/src/main.rs:1242 — in the "New event" window with a day/time asked, the cursor sits in the asked field, but `entered` only watches the title field: typing "28.10.2026" + Enter does nothing even once filled, while DEC-234 implies Enter saves once each field is filled → have asked_times report lost_focus+Enter of its fields and OR it into `entered` (new_event() already refuses while not ready)

crates/core/src/editor.rs:783, crates/app/src/editor.rs:711-725 — the "Day"/"Time" hints and the "Type the start date." / "Type the start time or choose all day." messages now apply to every event in the full editor (clearing the start of any existing event), not only to described ones; the story's technical note keeps the rest of MOD-05's window unchanged → limit to editors opened with an asked field, or record in DEC-234 that it applies to all events

crates/app/src/main.rs:2117-2128 — story edge case "offline, a named Google calendar → chosen as online, saving does not succeed" is handled only implicitly (no online filter in calendar_named) and no test covers it → add a test: offline, "w kalendarzu Praca" chooses Praca, no not-found note, Save refused with the offline reason

crates/app/src/editor.rs:587 — the quick-window path for a missing time (no guests, e.g. "Siłownia w sobotę"): asked_times' Time field, its focus and its All-day checkbox are not tested at app level (TC-10-32 goes through the full editor because a guest is named; only core QuickEntry::fill is unit-tested) → add an app test for the quick window with the time asked, filled and all day

crates/core/src/described.rs:365 — DEC-232 lets a part of the day alone ("Trening wieczorem") mean today instead of asking for the day; this matches the module AC and TC-10-11 but is the delivery loop's own reading of a must requirement (F13), with "Decided by: developer" → have the product owner confirm DEC-232

crates/core/src/create.rs:208 — the asked day accepts only the full regional numeric date ("28.10" is refused, see the create.rs unit test); TC-10-33 says "choose" a day; consistent with MOD-05's date fields but harsh for the one field the user must fill → optionally accept a day without the year, or offer the mini-calendar

raw:
US-10-05 meets its spec. All 5 acceptance criteria and all 6 covered requirements are met, each with a passing automated test. I found nothing blocking; there are 7 non-blocking findings below.

**What I ran on 98f0db8:**
- `cargo test -p calendar-core`: 474 passed.
- `cargo test -p calendar-buddy`: 227 passed. That includes TC-10-32…35 in `crates/app/src/description_asked_tests.rs` and the earlier TC-10-11 ("Trening wieczorem") and TC-10-13.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings`: clean.
- TC-10-18 against the fake model: date right 100 %, every field right 92 %.
- Ollama with `gemma4:e4b` is running on this machine, so I also ran the live test set by hand (`the_test_set_against_a_live_ollama`, TC-10-19). It passed with dates 96 % and every field 92 %, which backs up the hand run claimed in DEC-232. "Kawa z Bartkiem o 15", "Lunch o 13", "Lunch at 1pm" and both sentences that name a calendar were all scored right.

**Spec ↔ implementation**

| Item | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| #1 A given day or time is filled in; only a missing one is asked for | MET | `Described::missing` / `times` (`crates/core/src/described.rs`). TC-10-32 checks the day 31.10 is filled with the time empty; TC-10-33 checks 13:00–13:30 is shown with the day empty. |
| #2 A calendar is matched by its side-panel name, ignoring case | MET | `calendar_named` (`described.rs:295`) compares `trim().to_lowercase()` of `Calendar.name`, which is the name the side panel and picker show. TC-10-34 ("praca" finds Praca, "MY CALENDAR" finds My calendar) and a core unit test. |
| #3 Scenario: no time | MET | TC-10-32 steps 1–3: full editor on 31 Oct, time empty, cursor in the "Time" field, Save disabled; typing 11:00 gives 11:00–11:30 and enables Save; all day gives an all-day event on 31.10. |
| #4 Scenario: no date | MET | TC-10-33: day empty with the cursor in it, Save disabled; typing 28.10 enables Save; the fake Google receives Wed 28 Oct 13:00–13:30 in "Work". |
| #5 Scenario: a named calendar | MET | TC-10-34 (chosen, no note); TC-10-35 ("Prywatny" doesn't exist, "Święta w Polsce" is read-only) gives "Work" and the note `Calendar "<x>" not found — using Work`. |
| F09 | MET | `main.rs` `read()` picks the found calendar through `entry_in`; TC-10-34. |
| F10 / U06 | MET | `entry.not_found` is set only when a calendar exists. The note is drawn under the picker in the quick window (`main.rs:1229`) and in the full editor's Calendar row. TC-10-35. |
| F13 | MET | New kind `none`; `parse` returns `date: None`; TC-10-33. A part of the day alone still means today (DEC-232, see N5). |
| F14 | MET | TC-10-32; core tests for `QuickEntry::fill` and `Editor::from_quick`. |
| U07 | MET | Empty field with a hint, cursor placed in it (`ask` / `asking`), Save disabled via `entry.ready()` / `START_*_EMPTY`; TC-10-32 and TC-10-33. |

**Edge cases**
- Two calendars with the same name, first in side-panel order: tested in a core unit test (Google "Praca" is chosen before local "Praca").
- Disabled, hidden or read-only counts as not found: tested in a core unit test, and read-only also in TC-10-35.
- Offline with a named Google calendar: the code handles it (no online filter in `calendar_named`; the quick window's existing offline refusal then applies), but no test covers it (N3).

**Out of scope:** no violations. The prompt and schema changes (a `calendar` field and the `none` kind) are needed to deliver F09 and F13. Dropping the next-full-hour stand-in was anticipated by DEC-219. The small spill-over into the general MOD-05 editor is N2.

**The changed test-set sentence ("Kawa z Bartkiem o 15")**
- The change is consistent with the spec. The sentence gives an hour and no day, the same shape as the story's own "Lunch o 13" scenario. MOD-10-F13 and SRC-08-08 say the app then asks for the day, so the old expectation ("today", from the 2026-10-27 prompt's "today also when no day is given") contradicts a must requirement.
- The recorded answer changed from `same` to `none`. Under the new parsing the old answer would give no day too, so the expectation does not depend on the new recording.
- The live model scores the sentence right under the new rules.

**Constitution:** nothing violated. The matching, filling and timing logic is in `calendar-core`; the app only draws it. Gates are green.
